# Story 25 — Web language switch flips the interface without a reload (Story: CRM-37)

## Prerequisites

- **LANGUAGES-1-WEB (CRM-35)** completed: the two dictionaries in `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` and `I18nProvider` in `web/src/shared/i18n/index.tsx` are already in place, and `<html dir>` / `<html lang>` are already driven from a single effect there.
- **PLATFORM theming story (CRM-27)** completed: `web/src/app/theme-context.tsx` and its test are the shape this story copies. Do **not** invent a second pattern.
- Coordinate naming only (no code change) with **LANGUAGES-2-MOB (CRM-38)** and **LANGUAGES-3-WEB (CRM-39)** — they are out of scope here.

---

## Story Goal

The signed-in agent can switch the interface from English to Arabic (and back) from a control in the desk shell header. The switch changes text, writing direction and alignment **in the same render**, without a route change or page reload. The chosen language is remembered across reloads. Direction still comes from `<html dir>` and CSS logical properties — no second stylesheet mirrors the layout by hand.

**In scope:** stateful `I18nProvider`, persistence in `localStorage`, a header button in `DeskShell`, two new dictionary keys, a lint-style guard test that forbids `[dir=` selectors and physical direction properties in `web/src` CSS.

**Not in scope:** Android (CRM-38), locale-formatted dates/numbers (CRM-39), missing-key checker (CRM-40), any third language, run-time locale loading, changing the theme provider, altering shell layout, or translating any new copy beyond the switcher's two labels.

## Product rules (from story)

- **BR-6 — Two languages, always, in resource files, never hardcoded.** The two new switcher labels are added to `en.ts` **and** `ar.ts` in the same commit. No literal English or Arabic string appears in `DeskShell.tsx`.
- Signed-out visitors on `/sign-in` are **not** inside `DeskShell`. This story does **not** add a language control to the sign-in page. Rationale (record in the provider comment): the shared preference is still read on first render from `localStorage`, so a returning visitor whose last session was Arabic sees the sign-in page in Arabic already; a first-time visitor lands in English and can switch after signing in. Adding a second switcher on sign-in is a separate decision.

## Frontend Tasks

_No backend changes required._

### 1 — Make `I18nProvider` stateful and persistent

**File:** `web/src/shared/i18n/index.tsx`

Change the shape to match `theme-context.tsx` line-for-line where the concerns overlap:

- Add:
  ```ts
  export const LANGUAGE_KEY = 'support-desk.language';
  const LANGUAGES: readonly Language[] = ['en', 'ar'];
  const isLanguage = (value: string | null): value is Language =>
    value !== null && (LANGUAGES as readonly string[]).includes(value);
  ```
- Add `readStoredLanguage(fallback: Language): Language` that wraps `globalThis.localStorage?.getItem(LANGUAGE_KEY) ?? null` in `try/catch`, returns the stored value if `isLanguage`, otherwise returns `fallback`. Copy the exact prose of the theme comment (private window / stub / unrecognised value) — same reasoning, so same words.
- In `I18nProvider`, treat `language` as the **initial-value override**, which
  means it wins when it is given:
  ```ts
  export function I18nProvider({ language, children }: { language?: Language; children: ReactNode }) {
    // An explicit prop is a caller stating intent, so it beats storage. Only
    // when no prop is passed — which is every case in the application, since
    // App.tsx passes none — does the stored choice decide.
    const [current, setCurrent] = useState<Language>(() => language ?? readStoredLanguage('en'));
  ```

  **Corrected in review.** The generated plan wrote
  `useState(() => readStoredLanguage(language))`, which makes **storage win and
  the prop merely the fallback** — the opposite of what "override" means. It
  passes today only because the harness clears storage between tests, so a
  test's `language: 'ar'` faces an empty store. The moment a test toggles the
  language and then renders again with an explicit prop, it would silently get
  the stored value instead. Drop the `= 'en'` default so "given" and "not
  given" can be told apart.

  Either way this preserves every existing test that passes `language: 'ar'`
  (`web/src/testing/render.tsx:42`, and `routing.test.tsx` asserting
  `dir === 'rtl'`).
- Add:
  ```ts
  const setLanguage = useCallback((next: Language) => {
    try { globalThis.localStorage?.setItem(LANGUAGE_KEY, next); } catch { /* tab-only */ }
    setCurrent(next);
  }, []);
  ```
- Extend `Translation`:
  ```ts
  type Translation = {
    language: Language;
    t: Messages;
    dir: Direction;
    setLanguage: (next: Language) => void;
    toggleLanguage: () => void;
  };
  ```
  Derive `toggleLanguage` inside the `useMemo` (not in its own `useCallback`) so two quick clicks do not read a stale value — same reasoning as `toggleTheme` in `theme-context.tsx:57–59`.
- Update the `useMemo` value to `{ language: current, t: dictionaries[current], dir: directions[current], setLanguage, toggleLanguage: () => setLanguage(current === 'en' ? 'ar' : 'en') }` with `[current, setLanguage]` deps.
- Keep the existing `useEffect` that sets both `dir` **and** `lang` on `document.documentElement` — do not split it; a screen reader told the direction but not the language reads Arabic in an English voice.

### 6 — Guard: no hand-mirrored stylesheets

**Create file:** `web/src/shared/i18n/no-mirrored-styles.test.ts`

A Vitest test that walks every `*.css` file under `web/src/` and fails when any of the following appear **after comments are stripped**:

- Any `[dir=` selector (attribute selector on `dir`).
- Physical direction properties: `margin-left`, `margin-right`, `padding-left`, `padding-right`, `border-left`, `border-right`, and bare `left:` / `right:` declarations (not inside `background-position` etc. — restrict to a declaration at the start of a rule line).
- `text-align: left` or `text-align: right`.

Comment stripping must remove **all** CSS block comments `/* … */` (including multi-line) before scanning; do this with a single regex pass. The proof case is `web/src/shared/ui/tokens.css` line 73 which contains `[dir="rtl"]` inside such a comment and must still pass. Include a positive unit case in the same test file: feed a small in-memory string that contains a real `[dir="rtl"] { … }` block and assert the checker flags it.

Enumerate CSS files with `fs.readdirSync` recursively from `web/src/` (or `import.meta.glob('/src/**/*.css', { as: 'raw', eager: true })` if it fits the existing test style — check how `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` at `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` enumerates sources and match that pattern).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Private window / storage disabled** — `localStorage.getItem` throws. `readStoredLanguage` returns the `fallback` prop (default `'en'`). Enforced in `web/src/shared/i18n/index.tsx` inside the `try/catch` around the getter.
- **Unrecognised stored value** (e.g. a user typed `support-desk.language = 'fr'` in devtools). `isLanguage` filters it and the fallback is returned. Enforced in the same helper.
- **Rapid double-click on the switcher.** `toggleLanguage` is derived inside `useMemo` from the current `current`, not a captured stale value — same defence as `toggleTheme` at `theme-context.tsx:57–59`.
- **Reload persistence.** `useState` initialiser runs synchronously on the first render, so a returning Arabic visitor never sees an English flash. Enforced by not using a `useEffect` for the initial read.
- **Screen reader.** `<html lang>` is set alongside `<html dir>` in the same effect at `web/src/shared/i18n/index.tsx:30–37`; a plan to split them is rejected.
- **Comment containing the forbidden token.** `tokens.css:73` contains `[dir="rtl"]` inside a `/* … */` comment; the guard strips comments first, otherwise it fails on the very rule it enforces (L-13).
- **Signed-out sign-in page.** `DeskShell` is not rendered on `/sign-in`; the switcher is therefore not visible there. The provider still restores the last chosen language on first render, so the sign-in page appears in that language.
- **Existing tests that pass `language: 'ar'`.** The `language` prop remains an **initial-value override**; harness (`web/src/testing/render.tsx:42`) and every consumer (including `routing.test.tsx`'s `dir === 'rtl'` assertion) continue to work unchanged.

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend builds:** in `web/`, run `pnpm build` (or `npm run build`) — it must complete without TypeScript errors, proving the extended `Translation` shape is consistent with every `useTranslation()` caller.
2. **Frontend tests:** in `web/`, run `pnpm test` (Vitest). All existing tests pass; the new provider tests and the mirrored-styles guard pass.
3. **Frontend runs:** in `web/`, run `pnpm dev`, sign in, click the new header button; the entire shell flips to Arabic with `dir="rtl"` on `<html>` and no visible reflow flash. Reload the page; Arabic persists. Click again; English returns and persists.
4. **Regression — theme still works:** click the theme button after switching language; palette flips as before. `data-theme` and `lang`/`dir` coexist on `<html>`.
5. **Regression — sign-in:** sign out, land on `/sign-in`, confirm no switcher is rendered there and the page respects the last stored language.
6. **AI-attribution grep:** from repo root, `git grep -Ei 'co-authored-by:\s*(claude|gpt|copilot)|generated with (claude|copilot|chatgpt)' -- web/` returns nothing.
